gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.description: Every user is added by invite only, sent from Users. Households and budgets are created and access is granted from Users and Households & Access. A household member gets no budget visibility until an admin explicitly grants it, and a granted budget starts with no feature access until permissions are set.

managingUsersHouseholds.title: Managing Users & Households
managingUsersHouseholds.description: Deactivating a user blocks sign-in without deleting their history. Removing household access cascades: it revokes that user's access to every budget in the household along with its feature permissions. Revoking just one budget's access removes only that budget's permissions, leaving household membership and other budgets untouched.

payeeRenamingRules.title: Payee Renaming Rules
payeeRenamingRules.description: Payees are shared platform-wide, not per-household. A renaming rule matches an incoming or imported payee string against a pattern using one of four match types (Contains, Starts with, Ends with, Equals), then displays it under the canonical payee name. Merging two payees moves all transaction history, renaming rules, and per-budget auto-category mappings onto the surviving payee.

backupsRestore.title: Backups & Restore
backupsRestore.description: Backups are pg_dump snapshots encrypted at rest with this instance's encryption key (APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY). A completed backup can be downloaded from Backups. To move one to another instance (e.g. test to production): copy APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY to the target instance's .env first, since a few settings columns (SMTP password, VAPID key) are encrypted with it and won't decrypt under a different key. Then, from the app's checkout, run npm run backup:decrypt -- <downloaded-file> decrypted.sql, and load the result into a FRESH, EMPTY target database (the dump has no --clean, so it fails against a database that's already been through First-Time Setup): psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f decrypted.sql. Losing the encryption key makes existing backups unrecoverable, so keep it somewhere safe outside this instance.

docs.apiTokensDescription: Each user can generate their own read-only API tokens from their personal settings, for home-lab integrations (dashboards, monitoring). Every token is permanently scoped to exactly one budget, chosen at creation time, so a user with multiple budgets needs a separate token per budget. Tokens are unconditionally GET-only against a versioned /api/v1/… surface, rate-limited to 60 requests/minute, and capped at read-only even if the owning user has edit access. No write or webhook endpoints exist for tokens, by design. Send the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
